subject: Archaeology
title: The Caves of Lascaux
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Caves of Lascaux.

hook.text: In 1940, four French teenagers chased their dog into a hole and found a cave covered in 17,000-year-old art.

buildup.text: The cave walls displayed over 600 paintings of horses, bulls, deer, and abstract symbols in vivid color.

discovery.text: The artists used mineral pigments and animal fat lamps, painting by flickering light deep underground.

twist.text: After opening to tourists in 1948, human breath caused a green algae to spread across the paintings.

climax.text: Lascaux was sealed forever in 1963. Visitors now see an exact replica built next door.

punchline.text: The real Lascaux is locked. Only its copy is open to the world.

quiz.question: Why was the original Lascaux cave sealed to the public?
options: Earthquakes made the cave structurally unsafe
Human breath caused algae growth that damaged the paintings
Local authorities wanted to charge higher ticket prices

details.summary: The Lascaux cave in southwestern France, discovered by teenagers in 1940, contains stunning paintings of aurochs, horses, deer, and abstract symbols created around 17,000 years ago. The artistic sophistication of these Ice Age paintings challenged assumptions about prehistoric human capabilities.
details.whyItMatters: Lascaux proved that Ice Age humans possessed extraordinary artistic skill and complex symbolic thought. The paintings' beauty and technical mastery forced scholars to abandon the idea of prehistoric peoples as culturally primitive.
takeaways: Discovered by teenagers in 1940 in southwestern France
Paintings of animals and symbols created around 17,000 years ago
The cave was closed to the public in 1963 to prevent damage

faq.question: Why was Lascaux closed to visitors?
faq.answer: After opening to tourists in 1948, over a million visitors introduced carbon dioxide, heat, and humidity that caused algae and fungal growth on the paintings. The cave was closed in 1963. A replica cave, Lascaux IV, now provides the experience without risking the originals.

faq.question: What techniques did the Lascaux artists use?
faq.answer: They used pigments made from iron oxides and manganese dioxide, applied by brushes, pads, and blowing through hollow bones. They exploited natural rock contours to create three-dimensional effects. Some areas required scaffolding, showing deliberate planning and collaborative effort.
